cards.explanation: The answer is King of the Jews. The Magi, visitors from the east, arrive in Jerusalem and ask, “Where is the One who has been born King of the Jews?” (Matthew 2:2). They're asking about a newborn King. I'd have asked for directions too, friends, and then pretended I knew the way.
The answer is True. The Magi say, “We saw His star in the east and have come to worship Him.” (Matthew 2:2). They tell Jerusalem plainly why they've come. Worship is the reason they give.

The answer is disturbed. Matthew 2:3 says, “When King Herod heard this, he was disturbed, and all Jerusalem with him.” King Herod hears about a newborn King of the Jews, and disturbed is the word the text uses. I think I'd have dropped my whole tray, friends.

The answer is False. The text says Herod “…was disturbed, and all Jerusalem with him.” (Matthew 2:3). So Herod is not the only one who is disturbed. He has company, and it's a whole city carrying the same news.

The answer is where the Christ was to be born. Herod assembles the chief priests and scribes and asks “…where the Christ was to be born.” (Matthew 2:4). Notice he asks about the place, bakers. The answer comes right back in the next verse: Bethlehem in Judea.

The answer is prophet. The chief priests and scribes answer, “In Bethlehem in Judea… for this is what the prophet has written.” (Matthew 2:5). They go straight to what was written, friends. They don't guess, they point to Scripture.

The answer is their shepherd. The prophecy says a ruler will come out of Bethlehem “…who will be the shepherd of My people Israel.” (Matthew 2:6). A ruler and a shepherd in one. That's a title with some warmth in it.

The answer is time. Herod “…learned from them the exact time the star had appeared.” (Matthew 2:7). He wants the timing, and he gets it in a private meeting. I think when somebody asks for the exact time of anything, friends, it's worth noticing.

The answer is True. Herod says, “Go and search carefully for the Child, and when you find Him, report to me…” (Matthew 2:8). So the Magi are sent out with a job and a place to return. Keep that line in your pocket, bakers, because the story isn't done with it.

The answer is so he can go and worship Him too. Herod tells the Magi to report back “…so that I too may go and worship Him.” (Matthew 2:8). Those are his words to the Magi, friends, and that's the reason he gives.

The answer is over the place where the Child was. The star “…went ahead of them until it stood over the place where the Child was.” (Matthew 2:9). The star's stopping point is wherever the Child is. That's where the Magi's search ends.

The answer is rejoice. Matthew 2:10 says, “When they saw the star, they rejoiced with great delight.” Great delight, friends. That's more than a smile, that's the whole face going off like a firework.

The answer is True. Matthew 2:11 says, “…they saw the Child with His mother Mary, and they fell down and worshiped Him.” They came to worship, and they do exactly that. From the star to the floor, they follow through.

The answer is open their treasures and give gifts. After they worship, “…they opened their treasures and presented Him with gifts of gold and frankincense and myrrh.” (Matthew 2:11). Worship first, gifts next, bakers. That's the order the text gives.

The answer is return to Herod. The Magi are “…warned in a dream not to return to Herod…” (Matthew 2:12). Remember Herod's request to report back? The dream says no to that, friends. Notice they listen.

The answer is False. Matthew 2:12 says they “…withdrew to their country by another route.” After the dream, they take a different way home, bakers. Same journey, new directions, and no recalculating needed.
